new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Article)          List-II (Effect of National Emergency)
A. Article 250            1. Executive
B. Article 353            2. Financial
C. Article 354            3. Legislative
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Article 250 lets Parliament legislate on State List subjects (legislative), Article 353 lets the Union direct States (executive) and Article 354 lets the President alter revenue transfers (financial).
new.angle: U0325 #1 National emergency effects -> Articles 250/353/354

new.s:
Which of the following has shaped Centre-State relations in India?
1. Constitutional provisions
2. Conventions and judicial interpretation
3. Planning and party politics
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Centre-State relations are shaped by constitutional provisions, conventions, judicial interpretation, planning and party politics.
new.angle: U0325 #4 Factors shaping Centre-State relations

new.s: Under which Article of the Constitution did Kerala file its suit in the Supreme Court against the borrowing limits fixed by the Centre?
new.x: Kerala used Article 131, the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction over Centre-State disputes; the suit was referred to a five-judge bench in April 2024.
new.angle: U0325 notes gap: Kerala borrowing suit -> Article 131

new.s: What share of devolution from the divisible pool of central taxes have the States demanded (February 2026)?
new.x: States have demanded 50% devolution, against the 41% kept by the 16th Finance Commission.
new.angle: U0325 #6 Recent friction -> devolution demand

new.s: Which of the following is known as a 'Constitutional Emergency'?
new.x: President's Rule under Article 356, imposed on failure of constitutional machinery in a State, is called a Constitutional Emergency.
new.angle: U0326 PYQ ya2ab64df2f6 Constitutional emergency -> what it results in

new.s: Proclamation of which emergency allows the President to order a cut in the salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges?
new.x: Under a Financial Emergency (Article 360) the President can direct a cut in salaries of all government servants, including SC and HC judges.
new.angle: U0326 PYQ ya2ab64df2f6 Emergency -> consequence (salary cut)

new.s: In which Article does the word 'Cabinet' appear in the Constitution of India?
new.x: The word 'Cabinet' appears only once in the Constitution, in Article 352(3), inserted by the 44th Amendment for written Cabinet advice.
new.angle: U0326 #4 written cabinet advice -> Art 352(3)

new.s: What is the maximum period for which President's Rule can continue in a State?
new.x: With approval every six months, President's Rule can last at most three years.
new.angle: U0326 #1 President's Rule -> extension limit

new.s: In December 2020, the Andhra Pradesh High Court asked whether it could record a 'breakdown of constitutional machinery' in the State. Which Article of the Constitution does this relate to?
new.x: Breakdown of constitutional machinery in a State is the ground for President's Rule under Article 356.
new.angle: U0326 #2 AP High Court 2020 -> Article 356

new.s: Which agitation led to the first President's Rule in Andhra Pradesh in January 1973?
new.x: The first and longest President's Rule in AP (18 Jan - 10 Dec 1973) followed the Jai Andhra agitation.
new.angle: U0326 #2 First PR in AP -> context

new.s: Who became Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh when the first spell of President's Rule ended in December 1973?
new.x: The 1973 President's Rule ended on 10 December 1973 when Jalagam Vengala Rao became Chief Minister.
new.angle: U0326 #2 First PR in AP -> how it ended

new.s: When President's Rule in Manipur was revoked on 4 February 2026, who was sworn in as Chief Minister?
new.x: Manipur's 11th President's Rule (from Feb 2025) was revoked on 4 Feb 2026 and Y. Khemchand Singh became Chief Minister.
new.angle: U0326 #2 PR in other states -> Manipur 2026

new.s: By whom is the Inter-State Council under Article 263 established?
new.x: Article 263 empowers the President to establish the Inter-State Council; it was set up by a Presidential order of 28 May 1990.
new.angle: U0327 #1 Inter-State Council -> established by whom

new.s: Who chaired the 29th meeting of the Southern Zonal Council held at Tirupati?
new.x: Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister; Amit Shah chaired the 29th Southern Zonal Council meeting at Tirupati.
new.angle: U0327 PYQ yfe64e8e01c0/ye4a69a78db1 Zonal Council meeting -> chairman

new.s: In which State was the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council held in August 2026?
new.x: The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting was held on 20 August 2026 in Tamil Nadu, chaired by Amit Shah.
new.angle: U0327 #2 Southern Zonal Council meetings

new.s: On whose idea were the Zonal Councils set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
new.x: The Zonal Councils were the idea of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1956 and were set up in 1957.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: Zonal Councils -> whose idea

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that full faith and credit shall be given to the public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and every State?
new.x: Article 261 is the full faith and credit clause.
new.angle: U0327 #5 Full faith and credit -> Article 261

new.s: The full faith and credit clause (Article 261) of the Indian Constitution is modelled on the Constitution of which country?
new.x: Article 261 is modelled on the Full Faith and Credit Clause of the US Constitution.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: Article 261 -> source country

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Tribunal)          List-II (Year set up)
A. Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal      1. 2010
B. Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal       2. 1969
C. Second Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal 3. 2004
D. Mahadayi Water Disputes Tribunal      4. 1990
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Godavari 1969, Cauvery 1990, KWDT-II 2004 and Mahadayi 2010.
new.angle: U0327 #4 River water tribunals -> year

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over disputes between the Union and States, but does not cover inter-State river water disputes?
new.x: Article 131 gives original jurisdiction; water disputes are excluded because Article 262(2) lets Parliament bar all courts.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: Art 131 excludes water disputes

new.s: Which of the following was set up under Article 263 of the Constitution?
new.x: Besides the Inter-State Council, the Central Council of Health, Central Council of Local Self-Government and Transport Development Council are Article 263 bodies.
new.angle: U0327 #3 bodies under Art 263 vs others

new.s: The Mullaperiyar dam on the Periyar is located in Kerala. Which State runs it under a lease?
new.x: The 1895 Mullaperiyar dam lies in Kerala but is operated by Tamil Nadu under a lease.
new.angle: U0327 notes gap: Mullaperiyar -> location and operating State

new.s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The All India Services are criticised as violating the federal principle.
Reason (R): Their officers serve the States, but ultimate control over them lies with the Centre.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
new.x: AIS officers serve States but are under ultimate central control, which is why they are said to violate the federal principle.
new.angle: U0328 #3/#11 AIS violate federal principle (A-R)

new.s:
Consider the following:
1. Office of the Governor
2. All India Services
3. Planning Commission
4. Inter-State Council
Which of the above have been criticised as being against the federal principle?
new.x: The Governor, All India Services and Planning Commission are criticised as tools of central control; the Inter-State Council is a forum for cooperation.
new.angle: U0328 #3/#10 Institutions against federal principle -> identify from list

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the GST Council?
new.x: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment.
new.angle: U0328 #7 GST Council -> Article

new.s: What majority of the weighted votes is needed for a decision of the GST Council?
new.x: The Centre has one-third and the States two-thirds of the vote weight; decisions need a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.
new.angle: U0328 #7 GST Council -> vote shares

new.s: Who was the first chairman of the Administrative Reforms Commission set up in 1966?
new.x: The ARC (1966) was first chaired by Morarji Desai, later by K. Hanumanthaiya; M.C. Setalvad headed its study team on Centre-State relations.
new.angle: U0328 #1 Commissions -> chairman (ARC)

new.s: Which State challenged the NIA Act, 2008 in the Supreme Court in January 2020?
new.x: Chhattisgarh challenged the NIA Act in the Supreme Court in January 2020 as intruding on the States' police power.
new.angle: U0328 #6 Central agencies -> NIA jurisdiction dispute

new.s: What was the formal name of the Rajamannar Committee appointed by Tamil Nadu in 1969?
new.x: The Rajamannar Committee was formally the Centre-State Relations Inquiry Committee.
new.angle: U0329 notes gap: Rajamannar Committee -> formal name

new.s: Who among the following were members of the Sarkaria Commission besides its Chairman?
o: A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy
new.x: The three-member Sarkaria Commission had Justice R.S. Sarkaria as Chairman and B. Sivaraman and Dr S.R. Sen as members.
new.angle: U0330 #1 Sarkaria Commission -> members

new.s: In the case of a hung Assembly, what did the Sarkaria Commission recommend to the Governor?
o: Invite parties in a set order of preference
Call fresh elections without inviting any party
new.x: For a hung Assembly, Sarkaria said the Governor should invite parties in a set order of preference; Punchhi later endorsed this.
new.angle: U0330 #4 Article 356 -> hung Assembly
